false_match_lists: for K3, K4, K5, K7, K8: one entry per (same-element pair, other after element) with relation, before_k1, before_key, after_k1

ground_truth.normalized_outerHTML: recursive serialization <tag a1="v1" a2="v2">text<child/>tail</tag> with attributes sorted by name and inserted raw; void elements (area, base, br, col, embed, hr, img, input, link, meta, param, source, track, wbr) with no element children and no text render as <tag attrs> with no closing tag; comments/PIs render nothing but their tail text is kept; the element's own tail is excluded; then whitespace collapsed over the whole string and trimmed
ground_truth.rule: a before-element b and an after-element a are the same element iff normalized_outerHTML(b) == normalized_outerHTML(a) AND that string occurs exactly once among before elements AND exactly once among after elements
ground_truth.undetermined: before elements failing the rule (non-unique outerHTML in before, or no exactly-once match in after) and after elements left unpaired; counted, excluded from stability/false-match denominators

K1.example: html > body:nth-of-type(1) > div:nth-of-type(2) > main:nth-of-type(1) > ol:nth-of-type(1) > li:nth-of-type(7)
K1.pseudo: steps=[]; cur=el; while cur: parent=cur.getparent(); if parent is None: steps.append(cur.tag); break; sibs=[s for s in parent if s.tag==cur.tag]; steps.append(f'{cur.tag}:nth-of-type({sibs.index(cur)+1})'); cur=parent; if cur.tag=='html': steps.append('html'); break; return ' > '.join(reversed(steps))

K2.absent: key is null; null keys are never unique, never stable, cannot false-match, and are not covered
K2.pseudo: v = el.get('id'); key = v if v is not None else None

K3.pseudo: key = f"{tag}|{' '.join(sorted(class_attr.split()))}"; elements with no class get f'{tag}|'

K4.definition: tag + sha256 of whitespace-collapsed own text (direct text nodes only)
K4.pseudo: own = (el.text or '') + ''.join((c.tail or '') for c in el); key = f"{tag}|{sha256(collapse(own))}"

K5.definition: tag + sha256 of whitespace-collapsed full text content

K6.definition: K4 of the element + K4 of its parent + K4 of its grandparent
K6.note: parent/grandparent K4 looked up by their K1; <html> is outside the keyed scope so contributes the empty string
K6.pseudo: key = f"{K4(el)}|{K4(parent) if parent is an element with a computed K4 else ''}|{K4(grandparent) if grandparent is an element with a computed K4 else ''}"; for <body>, parent=<html> (no K4, contributes '') and grandparent is absent ('')

K7.definition: tag + sha256 of all attributes except class, id, style (name=value, sorted)
K7.pseudo: attrs = sorted([(k,v) for k,v in el.attrib.items() if k not in ('class','id','style')]); blob = '\x00'.join(f'{k}\x01{v}' for k,v in attrs); key = f"{tag}|{sha256(blob)}"; elements with no remaining attributes hash the empty string

K8.definition: K5 + the index of this element among siblings that share its K5
K8.pseudo: sibs = [s for s in parent if isinstance(s.tag,str)] (or [el] if no parent); same = [sibs_k1 for s in sibs if K5(s)==K5(el)] in document order; key = f"{K5(el)}#{same.index(K1(el))}"; index is 0-based

K9.definition: K1 with every nth-of-type index removed (the tag chain only)
K9.example: html > body > div > main > ol > li

normalization.attribute_sort: attributes sorted by raw attribute name string (lxml lowercases HTML names; namespaced attributes keep their '{ns}local' form)
normalization.class_list: value of the class attribute split on whitespace, sorted, joined with single spaces
normalization.collapse: re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text).strip() — every run of whitespace becomes one space, then trimmed

parser: Python lxml 5.2.1 (lxml.html.parse); elements = [<body>] + all element descendants of <body> (comments/PIs skipped)

rates.coverage: per key, per relation: (# before elements in the relation having the key) / (# before elements in the relation). Only K2 can be absent; all other keys exist for every element.
rates.false_match: per key, per relation: (# same-element pairs in the relation with before-key non-null and equal to the key of at least one DIFFERENT after element) / (# same-element pairs in the relation). A pair can be both stable and a false match when the key is correct but ambiguous in after.
rates.stability: per key, per relation: (# same-element pairs in the relation with before-key non-null and equal to after-key) / (# same-element pairs in the relation)
rates.undefined: any rate with a zero denominator is stored as null and excluded from summary medians
rates.uniqueness: per key, per relation: (# before elements in the relation whose key value occurs exactly once among before elements) / (# before elements in the relation). Absent K2 counts in the denominator, never the numerator.

relations.container_resolution: container path resolved as a K1 path in its source version (after for insert, before for remove, per structure.py); verified by child_tag child count against the event's before_count/after_count; fallback scans for exactly one element with the same K9 tag chain and expected child count
relations.event_positions: insert: event['positions'] are indices into the AFTER member list (members unmatched after insertion); remove: indices into the BEFORE member list (members unmatched before removal) — per 10-build-history-diffs/work/structure.py
relations.inside_group_after_position: group members at or below the event: insert — member j with Q[j] > j (shifted down by an insertion), where Q[j] is the after-position of the member matched by 10's (tag, id, text-hash) document-order rule; remove — member j with j in positions or some p < j
relations.inside_group_before_position: group members (children of the container with child_tag, before document order) strictly above the event: insert — member j with after-position Q[j] == j (unshifted), i.e. no insertion at or above its landing; unmatched members fall back to j >= min(positions) as at/below. remove — member j with no removed position p <= j (j not in positions and no p < j)
relations.outside_group_descendant_of_container: proper descendants of the container element that are not group members
relations.outside_group_elsewhere: all other elements under <body>, including the container itself; also the fallback bucket when the container cannot be resolved in before

scope: every element under <body>, body itself included
